new file mode 100644
index 0000000..77b7d3c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_key_panel_tooltip_alignment.py
@@ -0,0 +1,425 @@
+"""The key panel must not pad a tooltip that has no description in front of it.
+
+`render_description` in the key panel joins a binding's *description* and its
+*tooltip* with a single space.  When a binding carries **only** a tooltip there
+is nothing to join it to, so the separator must not be emitted: otherwise every
+description-less row is pushed one cell to the right of the description column
+and the panel stops lining up.
+
+Two completely disjoint palettes are exercised:
+
+* an *archive browser* whose bindings live on the **App** and whose panel is
+  raised through ``action_show_help_panel()`` (the ``HelpPanel`` route), at
+  160x40; and
+* a *query pane* whose bindings live on a focused **widget** and whose panel is
+  a directly mounted ``KeyPanel``, at 120x26.
+
+They share no key, no size, no widget tree, no wording and no binding host, so a
+fix keyed on any of those cannot satisfy both.  Every expectation is recomputed
+at run time from the bindings the live application actually reports -- nothing
+is transcribed from a screenshot or a stored baseline, and no snapshot is
+involved.
+
+Both a state view (the Rich table the panel renders) and a behavioural view (the
+text and segments the compositor actually paints) are asserted.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from rich.table import Table
+from rich.text import Text
+
+from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
+from textual.binding import Binding
+from textual.containers import Horizontal, Vertical
+from textual.widgets import KeyPanel, Static
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# helpers
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def _bindings_table(app: App) -> Table:
+    """The Rich table the key panel renders for the current bindings."""
+    panel = app.query_one(KeyPanel)
+    for node in panel.walk_children(with_self=True):
+        renderer = getattr(node, "render_bindings_table", None)
+        if renderer is not None:
+            table = renderer()
+            assert isinstance(table, Table), "the key panel must render a Rich table"
+            return table
+    raise AssertionError("the key panel does not contain a bindings table")
+
+
+def _cell_text(cell: object) -> Text:
+    """Normalise a Rich table cell to a `Text`."""
+    return cell if isinstance(cell, Text) else Text(str(cell))
+
+
+def _description_cells(app: App) -> dict[str, Text]:
+    """Map every keyed row of the panel to its description cell.
+
+    Group-title rows (which have an empty key cell) are skipped.
+    """
+    table = _bindings_table(app)
+    assert len(table.columns) == 2, "the bindings table has a key and a description column"
+    rows: dict[str, Text] = {}
+    for key_cell, description_cell in zip(
+        table.columns[0]._cells, table.columns[1]._cells
+    ):
+        key = _cell_text(key_cell).plain
+        if not key:
+            continue
+        assert key not in rows, f"duplicate key row {key!r}"
+        rows[key] = _cell_text(description_cell)
+    return rows
+
+
+def _title_cells(app: App) -> list[str]:
+    """The plain text of every group-title row (rows with no key)."""
+    table = _bindings_table(app)
+    return [
+        _cell_text(description_cell).plain
+        for key_cell, description_cell in zip(
+            table.columns[0]._cells, table.columns[1]._cells
+        )
+        if not _cell_text(key_cell).plain
+    ]
+
+
+def _own_bindings(app: App, action_prefix: str) -> list[Binding]:
+    """The non-system bindings this palette declares, as the app reports them."""
+    bindings = [
+        active.binding
+        for active in app.screen.active_bindings.values()
+        if active.binding.action.startswith(action_prefix) and not active.binding.system
+    ]
+    assert bindings, f"no active bindings for {action_prefix!r}"
+    return bindings
+
+
+def _expected_descriptions(app: App, action_prefix: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Recompute, from the live bindings, what each description cell must read.
+
+    A description and a tooltip are separated by exactly one space; when either
+    is absent the other stands alone with no padding.
+    """
+    expected: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for binding in _own_bindings(app, action_prefix):
+        description = Text.from_markup(binding.description).plain
+        parts = [part for part in (description, binding.tooltip) if part]
+        expected[app.get_key_display(binding)] = " ".join(parts)
+    return expected
+
+
+def _screen_lines(app: App) -> list[str]:
+    """Every line of composited screen output, as plain text."""
+    return [strip.text for strip in app.screen._compositor.render_strips()]
+
+
+def _column_of(app: App, needle: str) -> int:
+    """The screen column at which `needle` is painted (it must appear once)."""
+    hits = [(y, line.index(needle)) for y, line in enumerate(_screen_lines(app)) if needle in line]
+    assert len(hits) == 1, f"expected {needle!r} to be painted exactly once, got {hits}"
+    return hits[0][1]
+
+
+def _style_mask(app: App, needle: str, attribute: str) -> tuple[str, list[bool]]:
+    """The painted row holding `needle`, plus a per-column flag for a style attribute.
+
+    Styling is read back from what the compositor actually paints, so a fix is free
+    to build the cell out of spans, out of a base style, or out of anything else.
+    """
+    for strip in app.screen._compositor.render_strips():
+        if needle not in strip.text:
+            continue
+        mask: list[bool] = []
+        for segment in strip:
+            style = segment.style
+            flag = bool(getattr(style, attribute, False)) if style is not None else False
+            mask.extend([flag] * len(segment.text))
+        return strip.text, mask
+    raise AssertionError(f"no composited row paints {needle!r}")
+
+
+def _painted_flags(app: App, row_needle: str, attribute: str, target: str) -> list[bool]:
+    """The style flags of the columns that paint `target` on `row_needle`'s row."""
+    line, mask = _style_mask(app, row_needle, attribute)
+    start = line.index(target)
+    return mask[start : start + len(target)]
+
+
+async def _settle(pilot) -> None:
+    """Let the panel mount, compose and repaint before anything is read back."""
+    for _ in range(5):
+        await pilot.pause()
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# palette A -- archive browser, app-level bindings, HelpPanel route, 160 x 40
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+ARCHIVE_SIZE = (160, 40)
+
+
+class ArchiveApp(App[None]):
+    """Bindings declared on the App; panel raised via the help-panel action."""
+
+    BINDINGS = [
+        Binding("f2", "archive_rename", tooltip="Rename the highlighted entry"),
+        Binding("f5", "archive_refresh", description="Refresh", tooltip="Re-read the archive"),
+        Binding("f8", "archive_delete", description="Delete"),
+        Binding("f9", "archive_hidden", tooltip="Toggle hidden members"),
+        Binding("ctrl+t", "archive_tag", description="[b]Tag[/b] member", tooltip="Mark for extraction"),
+        Binding("ctrl+y", "archive_internal", description="Internal", system=True),
+    ]
+
+    CSS = """
+    #archive-body { width: 1fr; height: 1fr; }
+    #archive-listing { height: 1fr; }
+    #archive-status { height: 3; }
+    """
+
+    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
+        with Vertical(id="archive-body"):
+            yield Static("archive listing", id="archive-listing")
+            yield Static("archive status", id="archive-status")
+
+    def on_mount(self) -> None:
+        self.action_show_help_panel()
+
+
+async def test_help_panel_tooltip_only_cell_has_no_leading_space():
+    """A binding with a tooltip and no description gets no separator space."""
+    app = ArchiveApp()
+    async with app.run_test(size=ARCHIVE_SIZE) as pilot:
+        await _settle(pilot)
+        cells = _description_cells(app)
+        for binding in _own_bindings(app, "archive_"):
+            if binding.tooltip and not binding.description:
+                cell = cells[app.get_key_display(binding)]
+                assert cell.plain == binding.tooltip
+
+
+async def test_help_panel_all_description_cells_match_recomputed_text():
+    """Every row of the panel reads exactly as the bindings say it should."""
+    app = ArchiveApp()
+    async with app.run_test(size=ARCHIVE_SIZE) as pilot:
+        await _settle(pilot)
+        expected = _expected_descriptions(app, "archive_")
+        cells = _description_cells(app)
+        actual = {key: cells[key].plain for key in expected}
+        assert actual == expected
+
+

"The fix is confirmed. Every key now begins in the same column, so the panel reads as a clean vertical list, while descriptions, styling, tooltips, and section breaks are unchanged.

## Summary

**Root cause.** I pixel-analyzed the screenshot and found that the descriptions already lined up (all at the same column), but the **key column was right-justified** — every key shared a right edge while the left edge was ragged (`shift+tab` jutted out to column 0, `tab` sat at column 6, and `^q`/`f1`/`f2`/`^p` at column 7). So rows began in different columns rather than forming a clean vertical list.

**Fix.** In `src/textual/widgets/_key_panel.py`, changed the key column from right- to left-justified:

```python
table.add_column("", justify="left")   # was justify="right"
```

This left-aligns all keys to a single column. Descriptions still start after the fixed-width key column, so they don't move; `shift+tab` (the widest key) keeps its exact position; and all styling/content behaves as before.

**Snapshot tests.** Four stored SVG snapshots encoded the old right-justified layout. `pytest` and `pytest-textual-snapshot` aren't installed here (no network), so I reproduced the plugin's exact export path (`app.export_screenshot(simplify=True)`) and **proved it faithful**: with the fix reverted, all four snapshots regenerated byte-for-byte identical to the committed files. I then regenerated them with the fix applied:
- `test_help_panel.svg`
- `test_keymap_bindings_display_footer_and_help_panel.svg`
- `test_keymap_bindings_key_display.svg`
- `test_help_panel_key_display_not_duplicated.svg`

I also added a CHANGELOG entry under "Fixed".

One note for when you next run CI: I updated the snapshots by replicating the plugin's rendering rather than running `pytest --snapshot-update` (unavailable in this environment); I verified the replication is exact against the current committed snapshots, but it's worth a confirming `pytest` run on your end."
